I am p2 with $233 cash. I own two red properties with one house each. The other three properties have no houses.

p1 is in jail but still collects rent while there, so the orange monopoly remains dangerous. p3 owns a dark blue set with one house on Boardwalk and cash of only $76. Boardwalk with one house pays $200, and Park Place with one house pays $175.

p3 previously sold a house on Park Place to pay rent. They cannot build another house on Boardwalk until Park Place has one, so their dark blue set is currently weak. p4 has $754 and sits on Pacific Avenue. They have been offering increasingly for Ventnor, but I rejected those offers because they would immediately build the yellow monopoly and crush everyone.

I am weighing whether to trade. The safest choice is ending the turn and keeping p4 blocked. Building more houses on the brown properties would drain cash I need for survival and Indiana denial, and opponents rarely land there anyway.

p1 has $364, which is enough to hotel all three orange properties. They were sent to jail on turn 69, so they may have already built before ending their turn.

p1 cannot hotel the orange properties now because they are in jail. They would need to build during their next turn, which is post-turn or pre-roll. I have no way to stop them from doing so.

p3 is nearly broke with an undeveloped dark blue set. If they go bankrupt to p1's orange monopolies, p1 would gain both Park Place and Boardwalk.

Neither I nor p4 can reach the orange properties this turn or next. The distance from my current space to St. James is roughly 22 spaces, and from p4's Pacific Avenue it is about 35 spaces.

I am checking the standard Monopoly board layout to verify exact space numbers. p3 sits on Marvin Gardens (space 29), which is adjacent to the orange properties at spaces 26 through 29.

I had the orange property positions wrong. The correct spaces are St. James Place at 16, Tennessee at 18, and New York at 19. My earlier assumption that p3 was adjacent to the orange monopolies was incorrect.

Rolling a 12 from space 4 lands on St. James Place, which would cost $750 in rent. Even liquidating all buildings and mortgaging every property only raises cash to $723, so that risk is fatal. A roll of 11 would hit the Pennsylvania Railroad instead, which is manageable.

The St. James Place risk is too small to justify a bad trade. p4 will not land on the orange monopolies this turn, but they could hit my Pennsylvania Avenue for $26 or my browns if they pass GO.

I cannot build a full brown monopoly. Two more houses on each property would cost $200, leaving only $33. The brown set is too weak to threaten p4.

A brown monopoly would still leave me cash-broke if I hit rent. The red set is blocked because p4 owns Kentucky and needs Indiana from me. The yellow set is also unreachable since p4 holds both Atlantic and Marvin.

I will not complete the yellow or green monopolies for p4. A green monopoly would cost $200 per house, and I cannot afford to build on it with only $233. Without houses, the rent would be too weak to threaten anyone. I am now considering a trade with p3.

p3 will not trade their dark blue monopoly for anything. I cannot afford to develop it, and giving up my blockers would let p4 complete a yellow or green set.

I am now considering a trade with p1. They own Vermont and the orange monopoly, but their pink set is incomplete because St. Charles and States are mortgaged. Virginia Avenue is unowned, so they cannot finish pink without buying it and unmortgaging those properties.

I will not trade with p1. They are the current board leader and I should not help them.

Vermont is useless to me because I already own the light blue set.

Indiana Avenue is unowned and costs $220. I can buy it with my $233 cash. If p4 buys it, they would hold two red properties and need Illinois from me to complete the set.

I will not trade Ventnor, Penn Ave, or Illinois. I will buy Indiana to block p4 from completing the red set. I am checking whether p3 would sell a property to raise cash.

I rejected offering cash for p3's dark blue properties. That would break their monopoly and leave me with a single weak dark blue, draining my survival cash.

I am now exploring a trade with p4. Their holdings include three railroads, Oriental, Connecticut, Electric, Kentucky, Atlantic, Marvin, Pacific, North Carolina, and Short Line. I could use Kentucky to complete the red set, but p4 would demand Illinois or something more valuable in return. Railroads would only provide income, not a monopoly.

I will end the turn without building, mortgaging, selling houses, or trading. The brown properties currently pay only $10 and $20 in rent, so the cash would be wasted.

Building three houses on each brown property would cost $200 and leave only $33 cash. The expected rent from p4 landing there is roughly $12.5, so the return is far worse than the cost. A roll of 10 lands on Mediterranean Avenue, and a roll of 12 lands on Baltic Avenue.

Selling houses would only raise cash to $283, but that would reduce future rent without immediate benefit. Mortgaging properties is unnecessary since I have no debt and no urgent need for cash.

Mortgaging would cost 10% interest to unmortgage and reduce the value of any future trade. The current rent from those properties is small but free cash, so they should stay unmortgaged.

p4 could build five houses on the yellow properties for $750, leaving only $4 cash. Their total mortgageable assets would reach roughly $1689.

A three-house yellow set would generate $800 to $850 in rent, instantly killing every opponent. A two-house green set would yield $600 to $750, which is equally lethal. Any trade that gives p4 a complete monopoly is fatal.

Trading Illinois would still leave p4 needing Indiana to complete the red set, so it is equally dangerous as giving up Ventnor. I am now looking for a trade that lets me complete a monopoly while blocking p4 from building.
